hints: Notice the question asks for order of magnitude in $\text{Pa}$ for copper, which is a stiff metal that stretches very little under load.
Recall $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain}$ so a stiff material needs a very large stress of order $10^8 \text{Pa}$ to give even a small strain of order $10^{-3}$.
Compare the four powers of ten and ask which ratio $\text{stress}/\text{strain}$ gives a huge number much greater than $10^4 \text{Pa}$.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the typical power of ten for Young modulus $E$ of copper, measured in $\text{Pa}$.
State the rule: $E = \frac{\text{stress}}{\text{strain}} = \frac{F/A}{x/L}$, so it measures stiffness and is very large for metals.
Use typical behaviour: a copper wire needs a stress of order $10^8 \text{Pa}$ to produce a strain of only about $10^{-3}$ before yielding.
Estimate the ratio: $E \approx \frac{10^8}{10^{-3}} = 10^{11}$ with unit $\text{Pa}$, so the order is $10^{11} \text{Pa}$.

options.A: A value of $10^{-11} \text{Pa}$ is extremely small and would mean the metal deforms hugely under tiny stress, opposite to stiff copper.
options.B: A value of $10^{-4} \text{Pa}$ is still far less than $1 \text{Pa}$ and describes a very soft material, not a stiff metal.
options.C: A value of $10^{4} \text{Pa}$ is typical of soft rubber or very flexible material, far too small for the stiffness of copper.
options.D: A value of $10^{11} \text{Pa}$ matches the very large stress needed to produce a small strain in a stiff metal such as copper.
